absolute-value-misread.fix: A distance is never negative, and you can move that far on either side of the point you start from.

absolute-value-vs-order.fix: For lower or less, compare positions on the number line with their signs. For farther from 0, compare absolute values.

algebra-distributive-partial.fix: Draw arrows from the outside factor to EVERY term inside, then multiply each one.

area-scale-applied-once.n: Scaled the area like a length
area-scale-applied-once.fix: Change each side length to real units first, then multiply the sides.

averaged-unequal-groups.fix: Add the totals and add the counts (or the times), then divide once.

combined-unlike-terms.fix: Only terms with the same variable part combine. Circle each kind before you add.

commutative-overgeneralized.fix: Test it: compute both orders. Only addition and multiplication give the same answer after a swap.

compare-assumed-equal.fix: Close is not equal. Work out each value exactly, then compare.

compare-direction-reversed.fix: After you calculate, compare the two amounts again and say which one is greater in words.

compare-thought-impossible.n: Thought it could not be done
compare-thought-impossible.fix: Look for a step that puts both on the same footing: the same unit, the amount for one, or smaller pieces.

compared-without-computing.fix: Solve or substitute for every choice first. Then compare the results.

context-whole-units-ignored.fix: Ask what the answer counts. If it comes only in whole units, round the way the situation needs and check the real total.

coord-axis-point-misplaced.fix: x = 0 puts a point on the y-axis; y = 0 puts it on the x-axis. Points on an axis are in no quadrant.

coord-moves-combined.fix: Keep two running totals: one for left-right (x) and one for up-down (y). Use every move.

coord-quadrant-mixup.fix: Check each sign: x negative means left, y negative means down. Reflecting over an axis changes the other coordinate's sign.

coord-xy-swapped.fix: x comes first: move across. y comes second: move up or down.

decimal-division-unequal-shift.fix: Multiply the divisor and the dividend by the same power of 10, so the divisor becomes a whole number.

decimal-longer-is-bigger.fix: Compare place by place from the left: ones, then tenths, then hundredths. Add zeros so both have the same number of places.

decimal-not-lined-up.fix: Write the numbers so the decimal points sit in one column. Fill empty places with zeros.

decimal-place-names.fix: Say each place after the point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. A zero at the very end never changes the value.

decimal-place-value.n: Decimal point in the wrong place
decimal-place-value.fix: Estimate with whole numbers first. Then place the decimal point so the answer is close to your estimate.

distance-across-zero-subtracted.fix: Check the signs first. Same side: subtract the distances. Opposite sides: add them.

distance-coordinate-used-as-length.fix: Find the coordinate that is the same for both points and set it aside. The distance is the gap between the two coordinates that change.

divisibility-misjudged.fix: Divide and check for a remainder. A factor leaves nothing over; test the primes 2, 3, 5, 7 in order.

division-check-wrong-factors.fix: A check multiplies the quotient by the divisor. If you land back on the dividend, the division is right.

division-parts-misnamed.n: Mixed up the parts of division
division-parts-misnamed.fix: Dividend ÷ divisor = quotient: the dividend is split, the divisor says how, the quotient is the result, and the remainder is what is left.

division-quotient-missing-zero.n: Dropped a zero in the quotient
division-quotient-missing-zero.fix: Estimate the size first. Every time you bring a digit down, write a quotient digit, even if it is 0.

equal-sign-misread.fix: Read = as “has the same value as”. Find the value of each side and compare.

equation-answered-with-given-number.n: Reused a number from the problem
equation-answered-with-given-number.fix: Your answer is usually a new number. Put it back into the problem and check that it works.

equation-not-inverse-operation.fix: Name what is being done to the variable, then do the opposite to both sides.

equiv-bigger-bottom-bigger-fraction.fix: More equal pieces means smaller pieces. Write both as decimals or percents before you compare.

equiv-conversion-not-checked.fix: Convert the answer back to the form you started with. If you do not land where you began, it is not equivalent.

equiv-decimal-part-ignored.fix: Keep every digit of the percent. Write it over 100, then multiply the top and bottom to remove the decimal.

equiv-denominator-treated-as-100.fix: A percent is out of 100. Change the bottom number to 100 and change the top by the same factor.

equiv-forms-compared-unconverted.fix: Write every value in the same form, such as percents, then compare.

equiv-fraction-not-simplified.fix: When a question says simplest form, keep dividing the top and the bottom by a common factor until none is left.

equiv-fraction-scaled-unevenly.fix: Use the same number on the top and the bottom. Then check by seeing that the new fraction means the same amount.

equiv-nearby-benchmark-used.n: Used a close but different fraction
equiv-nearby-benchmark-used.fix: Close is not equal. Write the value out of 100, simplify, and check that it matches exactly.

equiv-percent-digits-split.n: Split the digits of the percent
equiv-percent-digits-split.fix: Keep the whole percent together and write it over 100 before you simplify.

equiv-percents-added-different-wholes.fix: A percent only means something with its whole. Try a real amount like 100 and work one step at a time.

equiv-rounded-treated-as-exact.fix: If a division never ends, a rounded decimal is only close. Use the repeating mark or the word about.

equiv-wrong-operation-for-conversion.n: Used the wrong step to convert
equiv-wrong-operation-for-conversion.fix: Fraction to decimal is top divided by bottom. Decimal to percent is times 100. Percent to decimal is divided by 100.

equivalence-judged-too-fast.fix: Equivalent means equal for every value. One value that differs proves they are not; a match at one value proves nothing.

estimate-rounded-poorly.fix: Round each number to the nearest friendly number (5 or more rounds up). Keep the same operation and the same divisor.

exponent-as-multiplication.fix: Write the power out as repeated factors, like 3⁴ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3, then multiply.

exponent-base-exponent-swapped.fix: The base is the factor that repeats; the exponent counts how many times. Evaluate both powers before comparing.

exponent-factor-count-off.fix: Write the base out as many times as the exponent says, then count the factors before multiplying.

expression-coefficient-constant-swapped.fix: Ask which number tells how many groups of the variable there are. That one sits next to the letter.

expression-context-misread.fix: Say what each number counts and its unit. A number next to the variable is per one; a number alone happens once.

expression-parts-misnamed.fix: Point to each piece: the letter is the variable, the number stuck to it is the coefficient, a number alone is a constant.

expression-quantities-swapped.fix: Label each number: what is already there, and what the total must reach. The total or limit goes alone on one side.

expression-term-dropped.n: Left out part of the rule
expression-term-dropped.fix: List every part of the situation, then check that each one is in your equation.

expression-value-used-twice.fix: Point to each number in the expression as you use it. Each one is used exactly once.

factorization-stopped-early.fix: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime number. Multiply them back to check.

factors-multiples-confused.fix: Factors divide into a number (they are not bigger). Multiples are what you get when you multiply it (they are not smaller).

figure-vertices-mishandled.fix: Go around the outside of the figure, and do the same step to every vertex.

fraction-decimal-mismatch.fix: A number has one spot on the line, however it is written. Change the fraction to a decimal by dividing, then compare.

fraction-denominator-dropped.fix: Write every number as a fraction, multiply tops and multiply bottoms, then simplify.

fraction-divisor-as-whole-number.fix: Dividing by 1/4 asks how many fourths fit. Dividing by 4 makes 4 equal groups. Picture both.

fraction-divisor-size-misjudged.fix: Compare the divisor with 1 and with the dividend. Smaller pieces fit more times; bigger pieces fit fewer times.

fraction-flipped-for-opposite.fix: Opposites and absolute value change only the sign. Keep the numerator and denominator where they are.

fraction-mixed-number-misread.fix: Read the whole number and the fraction together. The denominator tells how many equal parts make 1.

fraction-no-reciprocal.fix: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor.

fraction-part-whole-misread.fix: Say what each number counts: the bottom number is how many equal parts make one whole, the top is how many parts you have.

fraction-reciprocal-misformed.fix: A reciprocal swaps the numerator and the denominator of the divisor only. Check: a number times its reciprocal is 1.

fraction-straight-across-division.fix: Use the reciprocal method, or find common denominators first, so it works every time.

gcf-lcm-confused.fix: GCF: the largest number that divides both. LCM: the smallest number both divide into. List a few of each to check.

geom-area-changes-with-view.n: Thought the view changes the area
geom-area-changes-with-view.fix: The shape itself does not change, so its area does not change. Work it out both ways to see.

geom-area-formula-misapplied.fix: Say what each part of the formula does before you use it. Check the units: an area ends in square units.

geom-area-halved-wrongly.fix: Parallelograms and rectangles use base × height with no half. A triangle or trapezoid takes half only once.

geom-composite-piece-missed.fix: List every piece. Pieces that make up the shape are added; pieces cut out of it are subtracted.

geom-faces-edges-vertices-confused.fix: Touch each flat surface once as you count faces; edges are where two faces meet, and vertices are the corners.

geom-height-misidentified.fix: The height meets the base at a square corner. On a pyramid face, it is the slant height along that face.

geom-one-dimension-decides.fix: One long edge or one big face does not decide it. Work out the full area or volume of each, then compare.

geom-opposite-faces-misread.fix: On a rectangular box, each face has a twin directly across from it. Three pairs make six faces.

geom-perpendicular-misread.fix: Perpendicular lines meet at a square corner, 90°. Parallel lines never meet.

geom-regular-polygon-misread.fix: Check both the sides and the angles. From the center, a regular polygon splits into as many triangles as it has sides.

geom-rule-too-narrow.n: Thought the rule only works sometimes
geom-rule-too-narrow.fix: Test the rule on the case in front of you. Area and volume rules work for every size and angle that fits their shape.

geom-scaling-effect-misjudged.fix: Area uses two lengths and volume uses three. Work out the old and new values and compare them.

geom-solid-misidentified.fix: Prisms have two matching bases joined by rectangles. Pyramids have one base and triangles that meet at a point.

geom-surface-area-as-volume.fix: Surface area adds the areas of the faces (square units). Volume fills the inside (cubic units).

geom-triangle-area-no-half.fix: A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height. Multiply, then take half.

geom-unit-cube-size-ignored.n: Counted small cubes as cubic units
geom-unit-cube-size-ignored.fix: Count how many small cubes fit along each edge, then find what one small cube is worth in cubic units.

geom-volume-added-dimensions.fix: Volume counts cubes: layers of length × width, stacked height times. Multiply all three.

geom-wrong-measurement-used.fix: Label every measurement on the figure, then check that each number in your calculation is the one that step asks for.

graph-trend-misread.fix: Compare the y-values of the points at the same x, reading from left to right.

inequality-boundary-inclusion.fix: 'At least' and 'at most' include the boundary (≥, ≤, closed circle). 'More than' and 'less than' do not.

inequality-direction-flipped.fix: Read the inequality from the variable: x > 3 says x is greater than 3. Test one number.

inequality-graph-direction.fix: Pick one number on each side and test it in the inequality. Shade the side that works.

integer-order-by-size.fix: On a number line, greater is always to the right. A negative farther from 0 is smaller.

integer-zero-misplaced.n: Put zero in the wrong place
integer-zero-misplaced.fix: Every negative is to the left of 0 and every positive is to the right. Zero is neither one, and it is its own opposite.

lcm-not-common-to-both.fix: List multiples of both numbers. A common multiple must be on BOTH lists.

like-terms-power-added.fix: Adding like terms adds the coefficients only. The variable part stays exactly the same.

long-division-steps-mixed.fix: Repeat the cycle: divide, multiply, subtract, then bring the next digit down beside what is left.

measure-area-perimeter-swap.fix: Area covers the inside and is in square units. Perimeter goes around the edge and is in plain units.

measure-number-unchanged.n: Kept the number when changing units
measure-number-unchanged.fix: Ask which unit is bigger: the same amount needs more of a smaller unit and fewer of a bigger unit.

measure-rounded-factor-exact.n: Treated a rounded factor as exact
measure-rounded-factor-exact.fix: A rounded factor gives an approximate answer. Use ≈, and expect answers that are close, not identical.

measure-unit-size-misread.fix: Check the conversion fact before you use it, such as 100 cm in 1 m, 1,000 m in 1 km and 3 ft in 1 yd.

measure-units-not-matched.fix: Before you compare or answer, put every measurement in the unit the question asks for.

measure-wrong-unit-kind.fix: Length uses plain units (cm), area uses square units (cm²), and volume uses cubic units (cm³).

mixed-number-mishandled.fix: Turn the whole number into pieces of the same size first: whole × denominator, then add the numerator.

multi-step-stopped-early.fix: Reread the question. Ask: does my number answer exactly what it asks, for every item?

multiplication-fact-slip.fix: Check the fact by skip counting or by multiplying back. Close is not the same as exact.

negative-direction-reversed.fix: Negative means left of 0 on a number line and down on a vertical line. Check the direction before you move.

net-face-missed-or-doubled.fix: Name every face before you add: top, bottom, front, back, left, right. Check the count matches the solid.

notation-digits-joined.fix: Name the operation between the two numbers (add, multiply, power) and do it.

number-line-misread.fix: Find what one step is worth first. Then count the spaces from a labeled number, not the marks.

op-added-instead-of-multiplied.fix: Look for 'each', 'per' or 'times as many'. Equal groups mean multiply.

op-added-instead-of-subtracted.fix: Difference, distance and 'how many more' all mean subtract. Check that your answer is smaller than the larger amount.

op-added-or-subtracted-instead-of-divide.n: Added or subtracted instead of dividing
op-added-or-subtracted-instead-of-divide.fix: Ask: am I counting equal groups or making equal shares? Both are division.

op-divided-instead-of-multiplied.fix: If you know the size of each group and the number of groups, multiply to get the total.

op-multiplied-instead-of-added.fix: Ask whether the amount is added once or repeated in groups. Added once means add.

op-multiplied-instead-of-divided.fix: Sharing, splitting and 'how many groups' mean divide. Estimate: should the answer be smaller?

op-reversed-division.fix: Say it as a question: how many of the divisor fit into the dividend? The amount being shared goes first.

op-reversed-subtraction.fix: Check the order the problem gives. Then add your answer back to see if you get the starting number.

op-size-rule-overgeneralized.fix: Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes it smaller; dividing by a number less than 1 makes it bigger. Estimate first.

op-subtracted-instead-of-added.fix: Ask: do the parts join to make a total? If so, the equation adds.

op-subtracted-instead-of-divided.fix: Sharing into equal parts, or undoing a multiplication, is division. Check by multiplying back.

op-subtracted-instead-of-multiplied.fix: Each unit adds the same amount again, so the total grows. Multiply the rate by the number of units.

op-word-misread.fix: Sum: add. Difference: subtract. Product: multiply. Quotient: divide. 'Less than' subtracts from the number that follows.

operation-misread.fix: Read each sign again (+, −, ×, ÷) and say what it does before you calculate.

opposite-misread.fix: An opposite is the same distance from 0 on the other side. Keep the distance and switch the side.

order-of-operations-left-to-right.fix: Parentheses first, then exponents, then multiply and divide, then add and subtract.

parentheses-misused.fix: Ask what is grouped in the situation. Parentheses hold exactly that group, and nothing outside it.

percent-amount-ignores-whole.n: Ignored the size of the whole
percent-amount-ignores-whole.fix: The same percent of a bigger number is a bigger amount. Test with a small and a large number.

percent-base-not-100.fix: Say it out loud: percent means out of 100. Picture the 100-square grid.

percent-conversion-skipped.fix: Percent means per 100. Going from a percent to a decimal divides by 100; the other way multiplies by 100.

percent-discount-amount-slip.fix: Find the price after the first discount. Then find the percent of that price.

percent-discount-story-misread.fix: Reread the story and mark exactly what happens to the price at each step.

percent-discounts-added.fix: A second discount comes off the new price. Find each price step by step.

percent-extra-part-only.fix: Over one whole means the whole plus the extra. Count both pieces.

percent-forms-compared-as-written.fix: Change every value to the same form, such as percents, before you compare.

percent-over-100-denied.fix: 100% is one whole. More than one whole is more than 100%, like 1.5 wholes.

percent-part-and-whole-swapped.n: Swapped the part and the whole
percent-part-and-whole-swapped.fix: Ask: is the number I was given the whole or the part? Then choose multiply or divide.

percent-part-count-as-percent.n: Used the part as the percent
percent-part-count-as-percent.fix: A percent is out of 100. Rewrite the ratio so the whole is 100, then read the part.

percent-sign-as-operation.fix: A percent is a ratio out of 100. It names a part of a whole, not an operation.

percent-total-as-percent.n: Used the total as the percent
percent-total-as-percent.fix: The whole is the group you compare to. The percent tells how many out of 100 are the part.

percent-used-as-whole-number.n: Used the percent as a number
percent-used-as-whole-number.fix: A percent means out of 100. Write it as a fraction or decimal before you use it.

percent-whole-benchmark-missed.fix: 100% is exactly one whole. Compare the percent to 100% first.

percent-whole-cannot-be-rescaled.fix: Any ratio can be rewritten as an equivalent ratio. Multiply both terms by the same factor.

percent-wrong-part-named.fix: Underline which part the question asks about before you calculate.

percent-wrong-percent-used.fix: Reread the percent in the question and check your answer against it.

percent-wrong-whole-used.fix: Name the whole in the story first. It is the amount the percent is taken of.

perimeter-half-counted.fix: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths. Trace all four sides before you add.

pest-benchmark-parts-miscombined.n: Built the percent from wrong pieces
pest-benchmark-parts-miscombined.fix: Add or subtract your benchmark pieces and check that they total the exact percent you need.

pest-benchmark-percent-mixed.fix: 10% is one tenth (divide by 10). 1% is one hundredth (divide by 100). Say which one the question needs before you divide.

pest-benchmark-scaled-wrongly.fix: Write the percent as a sum of benchmark pieces, like 15% = 10% + 5%, and count the pieces before you calculate.

pest-discount-ignored.fix: Find what you will really pay: estimate the discount, take it off the price, and then compare.

pest-estimate-needs-calculator.fix: You can compare an estimate with the original numbers without a calculator. Ask which way each number moved.

pest-estimate-purpose-misread.fix: Ask what happens if your estimate is too low. When you must have enough, round so the estimate is high.

pest-estimate-treated-as-exact.fix: An estimate is close, not equal. Write both numbers side by side and see which one is larger.

pest-one-number-judged.fix: Check both rounded numbers. If they move opposite ways, you cannot tell from them alone. Compare with the exact value.

pest-over-100-part-dropped.fix: Split a percent over 100 into pieces, like 150% = 100% + 50%. Find each piece, then add them.

pest-percent-fraction-mismatch.fix: Turn a fraction into a percent by dividing 100 by its bottom number. Then check that it matches the percent you need.

pest-percent-sign-ignored.fix: A percent is out of 100. 0.5% is 0.5 out of 100, much smaller than 0.5 of the number. Check the size of your answer.

pest-rounding-direction-ignored.fix: Compare each rounded number with its original: up or down? Then think about what that does to the result.

pest-size-judged-by-digits.n: Judged size by number of digits
pest-size-judged-by-digits.fix: Reasons about high or low come from comparing the rounded numbers with the originals, not from how the answer looks.

pest-size-unchecked.fix: Do a quick benchmark check, like 10% of a friendly number, to see if the size is believable.

pest-whole-given-as-part.n: Gave the whole, not the part
pest-whole-given-as-part.fix: A percent less than 100% of a number is smaller than that number. Check that your answer is smaller than the whole.

pest-whole-rounded-poorly.fix: Round each number on its own to the friendly number closest to it. Check both.

pof-compared-percents-only.fix: A percent is a part of its own whole. Work out each amount first, then compare the amounts.

pof-compared-wholes-only.fix: A bigger whole does not always give a bigger part. Take the percent of each whole, then compare.

pof-divided-by-percent-number.fix: A percent of a number is a multiplication by the percent written as a decimal.

pof-guessed-close-not-exact.fix: Turn the percent into a fraction or decimal, then find the exact part. Close is not the same as exact.

pof-outputs-misread.fix: Line the amounts up in a list, then read them from greatest to least before you choose.

pof-percent-changes-cancel.n: Thought up and down cancel out
pof-percent-changes-cancel.fix: Ask what amount each percent is taken from. After a change, the next percent uses the new amount.

pof-percent-of-wrong-whole.n: Used the wrong whole for percent
pof-percent-of-wrong-whole.fix: Say which whole the percent is about. Divide the part by that whole to find the percent.

pof-percent-over-100-misread.fix: A percent over 100 is more than the whole. Write it as a decimal greater than 1 and multiply.

pof-percent-step-slip.fix: Write each step on its own line, say what each number means, and check each step before moving on.

pof-percent-wrong-decimal.fix: Percent means out of 100. Divide the percent number by 100 to get the decimal, and check the size of your answer.

pof-second-percent-from-original.fix: Find the new amount after each step, then take the next percent of that new amount.

pof-successive-percents-added.fix: The second percent applies to the new amount, not the starting one. Do one step at a time.

pof-whole-given-as-part.n: Gave the whole, not a part
pof-whole-given-as-part.fix: A percent under 100% gives a part smaller than the whole. Check your answer against the whole.

prime-factor-copies-miscounted.fix: Count every copy of each prime in the factor tree, and multiply your answer back to check it.

property-misidentified.fix: Match the pattern: what moved, what regrouped, what was multiplied, and did the value stay the same?

property-order-vs-grouping.fix: Commutative changes the ORDER of numbers. Associative changes the GROUPING with parentheses.

quotient-digit-off.fix: Multiply your quotient by the divisor. It should land on the dividend, with a remainder smaller than the divisor.

rate-not-per-one.fix: A unit rate is the amount for exactly 1. Divide the total by the number of units.

rate-wrong-count-or-rate.n: Used the wrong count or rate
rate-wrong-count-or-rate.fix: Find the rate for one unit and the exact count the question asks about, then multiply them. Check against a row you already know.

ratio-as-difference.fix: A ratio compares by how many times, not how many more. Write it as a : b and look for the scale factor.

ratio-compared-without-common-basis.fix: Find a unit rate for each, or scale both so one quantity matches. Then compare the other.

ratio-cross-products-misapplied.fix: Cross products multiply on the diagonals: the top of one by the bottom of the other. Equal products mean equivalent ratios.

ratio-graph-misread.fix: Each point is a pair: x counts one quantity and y counts the other. The point with x = 1 shows the amount for one.

ratio-graph-origin.fix: Equal ratios make a straight line THROUGH (0, 0). Check that y ÷ x is the same for every point.

ratio-inverted.fix: Match each number to its label. The quantity named first in the question goes first.

ratio-other-quantity-used.fix: Underline the item the question asks about, then use only that item's own numbers.

ratio-part-whole-mixup.fix: Say the ratio in words first. Part-to-part names two groups; part-to-whole uses the total of ALL groups as the second number.

ratio-scale-factor-wrong.fix: Find the factor first by dividing the target by the matching amount, check it, then multiply the other amount by that same factor.

ratio-scaled-additively.fix: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both parts by the same number. Check with a table.

ratio-scaled-one-term.fix: Both terms change by the same factor. Check the first term AND the second term.

ratio-simplified-partway.fix: After you divide, ask: do the two numbers still share a factor other than 1? If yes, keep going.

ratio-table-columns-out-of-step.n: Moved table columns out of step
ratio-table-columns-out-of-step.fix: Find how much each column grows from row to row, then move both columns the same number of steps.

read-question-missed-key-word.fix: Underline what the question asks for before you choose. Check that your choice answers exactly that.

reason-misses-the-math.fix: A good reason names the math idea that makes the answer true. Ask: does this reason explain why?

regroup-slip.fix: Work one column at a time from the right, then check with the inverse operation or an estimate.

remainder-misused.fix: The quotient is how many in each group or how many groups. The remainder is what is left over. Decide what the situation needs.

rep-forms-seen-as-different.fix: Each table row is a point on the graph and makes the equation true. Use each form for what it shows best.

round-down-when-need-enough.fix: When every part must be covered or filled, any leftover means one more whole item. Round up.

round-not-least-whole-count.fix: Round a decimal count up to the next whole number only, then check that one fewer would not be enough.

rounded-wrong-for-story.fix: Ask what the story allows: only full groups, never more than the limit, or enough for everyone. Then round to fit.

rule-checked-on-one-row.fix: Test the rule on at least two more rows. It must work for every row.

sign-dropped.fix: Decide the sign first: which side of 0 should the answer be on? Then find the size.

solution-not-substituted.fix: Put the value in place of the letter in the original equation. If both sides are equal, it is a solution.

solution-set-misjudged.fix: Exact amount: equation, one value. Limit like “at least” or “at most”: inequality, many values, including decimals.

stat-box-plot-misread.fix: Each of the four sections holds about one quarter of the data. The box is Q1 to Q3, and its length shows spread, not amount.

stat-center-vs-spread.fix: Center (mean, median) says where the data sit. Spread (range, IQR, MAD) says how far apart they are. Pair mean with MAD and median with IQR.

stat-data-miscounted.fix: Touch each data value once as you count, and check the total against how many values there should be.

stat-data-not-ordered.n: Did not order the data first
stat-data-not-ordered.fix: Before finding a median, a range or quartiles, list the data from least to greatest.

stat-fair-share-misread.fix: Find the equal share first, then ask what the question wants: the share, or how much moves to reach it.

stat-frequency-vs-value.fix: Decide first: does the question want a value on the axis, or a count of dots or a bar height?

stat-histogram-bin-misread.fix: Point to each interval the question names, read its height, and count every whole number from its first value to its last.

stat-histogram-vs-bar-graph.fix: Ask whether the data are numbers you can group into intervals. Numbers make a histogram; names or categories make a bar graph.

stat-mad-misread.fix: MAD is the average distance from the mean. A bigger MAD means the values are more spread out.

stat-mean-out-of-range.fix: A mean always lands between the least and the greatest value. Check your answer against both ends.

stat-mean-skewed-by-outlier.fix: Spot any value far from the rest. If there is one, the median describes a typical value better than the mean.

stat-mean-total-confused.fix: Total = mean × number of values. Decide which one the question wants before you calculate.

stat-mean-vs-median.fix: Median: put the values in order and find the middle. Mean: add them all, then divide by how many there are.

stat-median-middle-wrong.fix: Order the values first. With an even count, the median is halfway between the two middle values.

stat-mode-mixup.fix: The mode is the value that appears most often. The mean and the median are found by adding and dividing, or by ordering.

stat-one-value-for-many.n: Let one value speak for all
stat-one-value-for-many.fix: A typical value sits where most of the data are. Describe the cluster and the spread, not one far-off value.

stat-outlier-moves-wrong-measure.fix: Measures that use every value's size (mean, range) feel an outlier. Measures that use position (median, IQR) barely move.

stat-question-judged-by-surface.fix: Ignore the topic and the units. Only one thing decides it: will the answers vary?

stat-question-no-variability.fix: Ask: would different people or cases give different answers? If everyone gets the same answer, it is not statistical.

stat-question-vs-data.fix: The question is what you ask. The data are the values you collect to answer it.

stat-range-for-iqr.fix: Range = greatest − least. IQR = Q3 − Q1, the middle half only. The IQR can never be bigger than the range.

stat-range-misfound.n: Found the range the wrong way
stat-range-misfound.fix: The range is a distance: subtract the least value from the greatest value.

stat-shape-misread.fix: Find the long, thin tail. A skew is named for the side the tail points to; symmetric means both sides look alike.

stat-spread-misjudged.fix: Spread means how far apart the values are. Compare the gaps between values, not their size or how many there are.

stat-summed-instead-of-averaged.fix: A mean is a fair share. After you add, divide the total by how many values there are.

subtraction-sign-ignored.fix: Keep each sign with the term right after it, and carry it along when you combine or distribute.

term-dropped.fix: Before and after rewriting, count the terms. Every term must still be there, and a lone n counts as 1n.

u2-checked-digits-not-point.n: Checked the digits, not the point
u2-checked-digits-not-point.fix: After multiplying, estimate with friendly numbers. If the size is off, the point is misplaced.

u2-decimal-places-one-factor.fix: Count the decimal places in every factor and add them. The product has that many.

u2-mean-of-known-only.fix: A target mean tells you the total for the whole set. Find that total before you look for the missing part.

u6-exponent-covers-product.fix: An exponent belongs only to the number it touches. Work out the power first, then do the other operations.

u6-factor-from-one-term.fix: A factor you pull out must divide every term. Multiply it back through the parentheses to check.

u6-identity-effect-misjudged.fix: Test with a real number: 5 × 1 is still 5 and 0 + 4 is still 4. Multiplying by 1 and adding 0 leave a number as it is.

u6-split-with-one.fix: Split into two factors that are both smaller than the number. Splitting with a 1 leaves the same number behind.

u6-subtracted-before-multiplying.fix: Multiply and divide before you add and subtract, unless parentheses say otherwise.

u6-variable-on-wrong-quantity.fix: Give the letter to the quantity that everything else is described from. Then build the other quantity from it.

u7-line-spot-guessed.fix: Every fraction has one exact spot. Cut the space between the two whole numbers into equal parts and count.

u7-reflect-both-flipped.fix: One axis flips one direction. The coordinate that measures the distance to that axis changes sign; the other stays.

u8-equation-one-side.fix: An equation is like a balanced scale. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other side too.

unit-conversion-direction.fix: Smaller units mean more of them, so the number grows. Larger units mean fewer, so the number shrinks.

var-dependent-independent-swapped.fix: Ask which quantity depends on the other. The one you choose or control is independent; the result is dependent.

var-not-a-changing-quantity.fix: A variable is a quantity that can change. Say what it counts or measures, with its unit.

var-outside-the-situation.fix: Name the two quantities the problem pairs up. The answer must be one of those two.

var-relationship-missed.fix: If changing one quantity changes the other, they are related. Find the one that responds.

var-role-by-surface.n: Judged roles by the wrong clue
var-role-by-surface.fix: Ask: which quantity is chosen or changed on purpose? That one is independent; the one that responds is dependent.

whole-answer-not-checked.n: Did not check the answer back
whole-answer-not-checked.fix: Check backward: take the percent of your whole. If you do not get the part, the whole is not right yet.

whole-part-treated-as-whole.fix: Label the given number as part or whole, and say which percent goes with it. The number that matches the percent is the part.

whole-percent-added-to-part.n: Added the percent to the part
whole-percent-added-to-part.fix: The part already is a percent of the whole. Write part = percent × whole, then undo the multiplying by dividing. Check by taking the percent of your whole.

whole-percent-decimal-misplaced.fix: Percent means out of 100, so move the decimal point two places left. Then check that your whole makes sense for the percent.

whole-percent-taken-of-part.n: Took the percent of the part
whole-percent-taken-of-part.fix: Ask: is this number the part or the whole? A part that is less than 100% comes from a bigger whole, so undo the percent by dividing.

whole-smaller-than-part.n: Whole came out smaller than part
whole-smaller-than-part.fix: Compare the percent with 100%. Less than 100% means the whole is bigger than the part; more than 100% means it is smaller.

zero-reference-misused.fix: 0 is where you measure from. Ask how far from 0 the value is and on which side.
